upload.noDataHelpOverride: Leave this on Auto unless your data really does have terrain at {value} — a coastline at exactly 0 m, for instance. Then pick None.
upload.layersHelp: Your upload holds more than one survey. The top one is used wherever it has data; each one below fills what the ones above it left empty. Reorder them to change which survey wins where they overlap — newest first by default.
upload.gapFillStandardHint: Anything your layers don't cover comes from the global dataset, height-matched to your data at the seam.

disclaimer.title: Data Accuracy Disclaimer
disclaimer.lead: Please be aware that all terrain data, heightmaps and 3D models generated by MapNG are estimations based on available elevation, satellite and OpenStreetMap data, so they are only as good as those sources.
disclaimer.resolutionBody: Heightmaps are exported using the selected processing resolution to keep scaling consistent in game engines. When using the global 30 m dataset, terrain is still upsampled, so it remains smoother and less detailed than native high-resolution sources like USGS or GPXZ.
disclaimer.usage: This tool is intended for modding and creative use. It should not be used for navigation, engineering, or critical real-world planning.

about.title: About MapNG
about.subtitle: Real-world maps for BeamNG.drive
about.hero: MapNG turns any real-world location into a playable BeamNG.drive level: terrain, textures, roads with markings and traffic signals, buildings, bridges, vegetation and more, built in your browser or in the free desktop app for Windows and Linux.
about.whatBody: Pick a location, choose an elevation source and generate. The 2D preview shows what will be built, with relief, slope and height views; the 3D preview lets you look round. Then export a complete BeamNG level ZIP built from real elevation and OpenStreetMap data, or take GeoTIFF and GeoJSON data into your own workflow. Batch mode processes whole grids of tiles and can stitch them into one large level.
elevationItems: Global 30 m (AWS Terrain Tiles, mostly SRTM): the fallback where there's no lidar, or on its own; roads smoothed and levelled and rivers kept below their banks automatically; buildings, trees and viaduct decks taken out automatically
Best free, the default: Mapterhorn's free lidar where a national survey exists (much of Europe, Japan, Australia, New Zealand, parts of the US and Canada), the global 30 m elsewhere; no key needed
USGS 1 m DEM (USA: CONUS, Alaska, Hawaii)
GPXZ (global high resolution, with your own API key; faster on paid plans)
Your own uploads: LAZ/LAS point clouds, GeoTIFF, ASC, GML/XML (also zipped), layered and reprojected, with gaps filled from the global 30 m or GPXZ and blended seams
previewItems: 2D preview: what will be built, by group, with relief, slope and height views and contour lines
Satellite, OSM, hybrid, Game Texture or plain terrain
3D buildings, trees, bushes and barriers from OSM
Mesh quality from balanced up to full native detail
exportItems: BeamNG level package (.zip), up to 16384 x 16384
GeoTIFF elevation (WGS84 or the source CRS)
Advanced mode and Batch mode (per tile) add: 16-bit heightmaps, satellite, OSM, hybrid and Game Texture images, road masks, GLB, DAE and .ter
osmItems: MapNG's own OSM copy, growing region by region toward the whole planet: fast, and unaffected by Overpass outages
Show MapNG OSM coverage outlines those regions on the map
Everywhere else: health-ranked Overpass mirrors with an edge cache
Bring your own Overpass server (Tracestrack, Overspan); MapNG's copy still answers first where it can
A banner tells you when the public Overpass servers are down
Overture Maps adds building heights and the footprints OSM is missing (on by default, under Include OSM features)
If every Overpass server fails, OSM data comes from Overture Maps' monthly release instead, so exports still work
about.resolutionStrong: Output sizes from 512 to 16384 px at any processing scale (m/px).
about.resolutionBody: At 1 m/px that covers 0.26 km² up to 268 km². Global 30 m elevation is upsampled and its roads are smoothed automatically; USGS, GPXZ, NMT and uploads keep their real detail.
about.batchIntro: Process large areas as a grid of tiles (up to 20 x 20). Each tile is generated in turn and its selected exports are packaged into its own ZIP. Features include:
batchItems: Combined BeamNG level: stitch a 2 x 2, 4 x 4 or 8 x 8 grid into one playable level (up to 16384 px)
Configurable grid size, resolution and export selection
Per-tile X/Y offsets with live drag editing on the map
Tiles Follow Map Center for center-anchored or world-locked layouts
Shared elevation baseline and a stitched 16-bit verification heightmap
Live progress with a color-coded tile grid and satellite thumbnails
Pause, resume and retry failed tiles; state survives a reload
GPXZ concurrent requests on paid plans
about.beamngBody: A ready-to-drive level ZIP for BeamNG.drive 0.40, built from the real place:
beamngItems: Terrain painted with materials from OSM land use, and from ESA WorldCover land cover where OSM maps none, with a 2x satellite or Game base texture (its water straight from the satellite image, its snow where the land cover has it) you can touch up before export
A regional look chosen from the location and from what covers the land: grass, ground cover, rocks and water
Regional trees from BeamNG's own models, picked from OSM tags and the local climate, planted only where WorldCover sees tree cover (trees OSM maps one by one always stand)
Textured buildings with BeamNG's facades and roofs
DecalRoads with real surfaces, lane markings by country, crosswalks, stop bars, parking lanes and shoulders
Raised sidewalks with curb returns and ramps, and median islands on divided roads
Traffic signals for every approach, road signs, and street lamps that light up at night
Hydrants, bins, benches, utility poles and power lines
Bridges with solved decks, piers and graded abutments; tunnels with portals and lights; concrete arch dams with the road and guardrails along the crest
AI traffic on the road network, road names on the minimap, and fuel stations
A surrounding backdrop and a detailed export_report.txt for troubleshooting
A "How heavy is this level?" check before you export, with BeamNG's size and precision limits (it only warns)
additionalItems: Share your whole setup: a short code or link (works for 24 hours), a long code that never expires, or a file. Paste one on the map to load it; your own keys and servers never go with it
Location search (Nominatim), preset scenic locations and Use my location

Keyless Esri satellite and topo layers (place and road names on satellite), one world with a border at the date line, a scale bar, cursor and crosshair coordinates, a right-click menu, and Ctrl+scroll to zoom on the crosshair
Stage-by-stage progress cards for generation and export, with finished steps and timings
Generation caching and cancel for long-running tasks
Light and dark mode, in 7 languages
Export hotspots: an opt-in glow map of where people export levels
Expand all / Collapse all for the settings sections

tech.title: MapNG Tech Stack
tech.footer1: Built to assist with BeamNG.drive modding workflows.
tech.footer2: Open-source tooling for real-world terrain workflows.

core.name: Vue 3
core.desc: Composition API and reactive state management

core.name: JavaScript (ES6+)
core.desc: Modern standard with modules, async/await, and worker messaging

core.name: Tailwind CSS
core.desc: Utility-first styling with dark mode support

core.name: Vite
core.desc: Fast dev server and optimized production builds

core.name: Reactive Local State
core.desc: Pinia plus Vue refs/computed with localStorage persistence

core.name: Noto Sans and Overpass
core.desc: BeamNG.drive's own interface fonts, bundled (SIL Open Font License)

render.name: Three.js
render.desc: WebGL 3D engine: geometry, materials, textures, export

render.name: TresJS
render.desc: Declarative Vue 3 renderer for Three.js scenes

render.name: Cascaded Shadow Maps
render.desc: 4-cascade CSM with 2048 px shadow maps and soft PCF filtering

render.name: HDR Environment
render.desc: 4K puresky HDRI for realistic ambient and reflection lighting

render.name: Collada and GLTF exporters
render.desc: BeamNG DAE shapes (buildings, bridges, sidewalks, power lines, backdrop), and GLB/DAE models in Advanced mode and batch

map.name: Leaflet and Vue-Leaflet
map.desc: Interactive 2D map with keyless Esri satellite, topo and label layers, dark mode and OSM coverage outlines

map.name: proj4 and GeoTIFF
map.desc: CRS reprojection (incl. conic/UTM uploads), DEM parsing and GeoTIFF export

map.name: Local Transverse Mercator
map.desc: Custom metric projection for pixel-aligned processing grids

map.name: Nominatim Geocoding
map.desc: Dual-endpoint search plus reverse lookup for suggested BeamNG level names

map.name: PMTiles
map.desc: Reads MapNG's own OpenStreetMap archives straight from Cloudflare R2 with range requests

tex.name: HTML5 Canvas API
tex.desc: Procedural texture generation up to 8192x8192 with OSM land-use, roads, and overlays

tex.name: fast-png
tex.desc: 16-bit precision heightmap and road mask encoding

tex.name: OSM Lane Renderer
tex.desc: Procedural road overlays, junction fills, crosswalk hints, and smoothed curves

tex.name: Web Workers

src.name: AWS Terrain Tiles
src.desc: Global 30 m elevation, mostly SRTM (Terrarium encoding at z15): the fallback where there's no lidar

src.name: Mapterhorn
src.desc: Free terrain tiles from 155 open national and global elevation sources (Terrarium WebP, up to z17)

src.name: GEDTM30 (OpenGeoHub)
src.desc: Global 30 m bare-earth terrain model (CC-BY 4.0), used to find the ground under buildings and trees in the global 30 m

src.name: Copernicus GLO-30
src.desc: Second global 30 m model (2011–2015, EU/ESA, via Mapterhorn), averaged in by the ground filter

src.name: ESA WorldCover
src.desc: Global 10 m land cover (2021, CC BY 4.0), read while generating: trees only where it sees tree cover, ground materials and grass on land OSM doesn't map, snow on the game texture, and the regional look

src.name: USGS National Map
src.desc: 1m DEM via TNM Access API (CONUS, Alaska, Hawaii)

src.name: GPXZ API
src.desc: Global hi-res elevation with your own key: auto-chunking, rate-limit probing and concurrent requests on paid plans

src.name: Custom Elevation Upload
src.desc: Bring-your-own DEM: LAZ/LAS point clouds (laz-perf WASM), GeoTIFF (geotiff), ASC grids, and GML/XML (fast-xml-parser) - single or multi-tile, reprojected to the output grid

src.name: Esri World Imagery
src.desc: High-res satellite textures, zoom chosen to match the base texture (around z17, ~1.2 m/px)

src.name: OpenStreetMap
src.desc: MapNG's own OSM archive on Cloudflare R2 (PMTiles, read by range), health-ranked Overpass mirrors with an edge cache, or your own Overpass server, with Overture Maps as a last resort

src.name: Overture Maps
src.desc: Building heights and footprints OSM lacks (Microsoft and Google detected, national cadastres), and all map data when OpenStreetMap's Overpass servers are down; from tiles.overturemaps.org (ODbL / CDLA)

src.name: JSZip
src.desc: Client-side ZIP packaging for BeamNG levels and batch jobs, streamed to disk (OPFS) for large levels

src.name: Blob URL Management
src.desc: Binary handling for large textures, heightmaps, and packaged exports

src.name: USGS 3DEP lidar
src.desc: Measured bridge deck heights in the USA, from the public lidar archive

src.name: iNaturalist
src.desc: Which tree species grow in the area, for each export's tree mix

deploy.name: Cloudflare Workers
deploy.desc: Edge-hosted site and /api routes (OSM cache, OSM tiles from R2, proxies, hotspots, settings stats, send codes, problem reports), deployed per branch by Workers Builds

deploy.name: Cloudflare R2 and Durable Objects
deploy.desc: MapNG's OSM archives, send codes and problem reports (R2); export hotspots and settings stats (a Durable Object)

deploy.name: Electron
deploy.desc: MapNG Desktop for Windows and Linux: a bundled Node runtime for generating and exporting on every CPU core, with electron-updater for updates you agree to, free lidar at full detail for big areas, and a download cache while you change settings

privacy.title: How export sharing works
privacy.intro: Sharing is off unless you turn it on. When it's on, MapNG counts where levels are exported, so everyone can see the busy areas on the hotspot map.
privacy.sent: For each level you export: which ~5 km square of the map it's in, and whether it came from the website or the desktop app. The square is worked out on your own computer, so your exact location never leaves it.
privacy.notSent: No name, account, email or device ID. No level name, settings or map data. No exact coordinates. Your IP address is not stored.
privacy.where: In MapNG's own Cloudflare account, in a small database (a Cloudflare Durable Object) that only the MapNG developer can access. Like every request to mapng.com, reports pass through Cloudflare's network.
privacy.how: One row per ~5 km square: how many exports came from the website, how many from the desktop app, and the date of the latest one. Nothing links a row to the people who exported there. To stop spam, the server briefly keeps a scrambled (hashed) form of your IP address in memory to allow at most 30 reports an hour; it is never written to storage and is gone within the hour.
privacy.use: Only for the hotspot map: the counts per square are what the overlay draws, and anyone can turn it on. The MapNG developer looks at the same totals to see where MapNG is used, for example to choose which regions get MapNG's own faster OSM data next.
privacy.never: Your data is never sold, never shared with anyone, and never used for advertising or tracking. The only place it ever appears is the hotspot map, as totals per square.
privacy.control: Turn sharing on or off at any time with "Share my exports" in the Map layers box on the map. Turning it off stops reports straight away. Counts already added can't be traced back to you, so they can't be picked out and removed individually.
privacy.readMore: Read the full details: exact data, pipeline and code

report.intro: Send a report to help fix it? It goes privately to the MapNG developer, and nothing is sent unless you choose Send.

report.incDump: A crash snapshot ({kb} KB): part of what MapNG had in memory when it crashed, which shows where it failed. It can include things like file paths.
report.incNever: Never included: your name or account, your files, the level itself, or anything else on your computer.
report.privacy: How reports are stored and used
report.sentHint: Mention this ID on Discord or GitHub if you'd like an answer about it.
report.incConfig: Your settings, as a code (it includes the location, so it goes when you untick it)
report.introLevel: Send {name}'s export report to help with a problem? It goes privately to the MapNG developer, and nothing is sent unless you choose Send.
report.incExportReport: This level's export report ({kb} KB): its settings, what was built, the checks and the export's log. It names the place, its coordinates and its streets.

usage.askBody: MapNG can count which export settings people pick (like Game Texture, or terrain edits off), so the developer knows what to improve and what nobody uses. Only the settings are sent: never the location, level name or anything about you. Change it any time in the Map layers box.
usage.shareToggle: Share which settings I use (no location)
usage.welcome: Share which export settings I use (never where), anonymously, to help decide what to improve

terrainChoice.title: Terrain
terrainChoice.subtitle: how much MapNG shapes the elevation
terrainChoice.readyHint30: Global 30 m: buildings and trees taken out of the ground, rivers and roads levelled in, fine ground detail and sharp cliffs. Lidar and GPXZ: roads aligned, nothing else.
terrainChoice.readyHintFine: Roads aligned with your elevation and levelled at bridges, tunnels and sidewalks. Where the global 30 m fills in, it also gets buildings and trees taken out, rivers and roads levelled, fine detail and cliffs.
terrainChoice.customHint: Choose each edit yourself, when generating and in the level export.
terrainChoice.untouchedHint: The elevation exactly as downloaded: no edits at all. Tunnels open only their entrances, with big portals hiding the cut.
terrainChoice.untouchedWarn: On the global 30 m, buildings and trees stay as lumps in the ground, roads follow every bump, and tunnels whose entrances would need digging are not built (their roads go over the hill).
terrainChoice.basicNote: Terrain: Ready to drive (buildings and trees taken out of 30 m data, roads levelled in). Switch to Advanced to change it.
terrainChoice.genGroundFilterHint: Global 30 m only: buildings, woods and viaduct decks taken out
terrainChoice.genLowerWaterHint: Global 30 m only: it reads the tree tops along rivers
terrainChoice.genSmoothRoadsHint: Level across, smooth along, joined at junctions

osmFile.title: Use your own OSM file
osmFile.hint: Fresher data, or no OpenStreetMap server reachable? Pull this area straight from openstreetmap.org, or drop an .osm file here. While it covers the area, MapNG reads it instead of fetching.
osmFile.downloadTitle: Save this area's OpenStreetMap data as an .osm file (you choose where; Downloads to start with)
osmFile.tooBig: Too big for one openstreetmap.org export (at most 0.25 square degrees and 50,000 points). Make the area smaller, or save the area from JOSM.
osmFile.drop: Drop the .osm file here, or click to choose
osmFile.bad: This file could not be read as OpenStreetMap data.
osmFile.coverage_full: Covers the whole area: used instead of the OSM servers.
osmFile.coverage_partial: Covers {pct}% of the area: used, and the rest of the area gets no map data.
osmFile.coverage_none: Doesn't cover this area: not used. Map data is fetched as usual.
osmFile.coverage_partialGrid: Covers {pct}% of the grid: tiles it reaches use it, the others download their map data as usual.
osmFile.pullTitle: Fetch this area from openstreetmap.org and use it right away (the same data as its Export button)
osmFile.openSiteTitle: Open openstreetmap.org's Export page with this area selected
osmFile.limitNote: openstreetmap.org hands out at most 50,000 points per export: about 1 km² of a dense town, much more of the countryside.
osmFile.err_too_big: Too much data for one openstreetmap.org export (over 50,000 points). Make the area smaller, or save it from JOSM.
osmFile.err_busy: openstreetmap.org is busy right now. Try again in a minute.
osmFile.err_network: openstreetmap.org could not be reached. Check your connection, or use View on OSM.
osmFile.err_http: openstreetmap.org couldn't hand out this area. Hover for details.
osmFile.policyNote: Pull and Download send one request per click to openstreetmap.org's API, which is meant for editing rather than read-only use. You are responsible for following its usage policy.

wizard.reviewHint: Generate gets the terrain and the map data, then opens a preview. Click a line to change it.
wizard.runHint: Start generates and exports every tile in one go, with nothing to preview in between. Click a line to change it.
wizard.generated: Terrain ready: it matches these settings.
wizard.generatedStale: Settings changed since generating: generate again to use them.
wizard.exportStale: Your settings changed since this terrain was generated. Exporting now uses the old terrain (its elevation source and Terrain choice). Generate again to use the new settings.
wizard.exportStaleShort: This export uses the terrain generated with your earlier settings.

spawnPoints.title: Spawn & quicktravel points
spawnPoints.intro: Pick where the car starts and add places to jump to. In BeamNG they show in the big map's Points of Interest under Quicktravel Points, each with a photo.
spawnPoints.placeHint: Click the map to drop a point; drag before letting go to aim it. Drag a pin to move it, or the white handle at its arrow to turn it.
spawnPoints.empty: Automatic: the car starts on a road near the middle of the map.
spawnPoints.name: Name
spawnPoints.heading: Heading (0° = north)
spawnPoints.noDefault: No point is the spawn (★): the car starts on a road near the middle, as without points.
spawnPoints.snapNote: Each point moves onto the nearest drivable road when exported (bridges and tunnels too) and faces along it; away from roads it stays where placed and faces its arrow.

backgroundAreas.title: Background areas
backgroundAreas.intro: Shade the hills you won't drive. They keep their shape but get no buildings, trees, grass or props, and download at lower detail. Draw lines (the map's edge counts as part of an outline), then shade the closed areas, or keep the roads you'll drive.
backgroundAreas.roadsLoading: Finding the roads in this area…
backgroundAreas.roadsFailed: Couldn't load the roads. Try again, or draw lines instead.
backgroundAreas.roadsNone: No drivable roads mapped in this area.
backgroundAreas.locked: The area box is locked while background areas exist. Remove all of them to move or resize it.
backgroundAreas.lockBody: Background areas use the box's edges as part of their outlines, and the data is fetched for this exact square. While any exist:
backgroundAreas.lockPoint1: the box can't be moved or resized, and its size and m/px are fixed;
backgroundAreas.lockPoint2: you can still pan and zoom the map to draw;
backgroundAreas.lockPoint3: removing all of them unlocks it.
backgroundAreas.hintLine: Draw from edge to edge, or a closed loop. Hold Space to pan.
backgroundAreas.hintBucket: Click a closed area to make it background.
backgroundAreas.hintErase: Click a line or an Unmask stroke to delete it.
backgroundAreas.hintRoad: Click the roads you'll drive. Everything farther than the width from them becomes background.
backgroundAreas.hintOpen: This line doesn't close an area: end it on the box's edge or another line.
backgroundAreas.hintClosed: Closed. Use Shade area to make an area background.
backgroundAreas.hintShade: Click to make this area background.
backgroundAreas.hintUnshade: Click to make this area drivable again.
backgroundAreas.hintNoAreas: No closed areas yet: draw a line first.
backgroundAreas.hintWhole: That area is the whole map: draw a line that closes it first.
backgroundAreas.hintRoadOn: Keeping {name}: {width} m on each side stays drivable.
backgroundAreas.staleCleared: The background areas were drawn for a box that has since moved, so they were removed.
backgroundAreas.unmaskShift: Hold Shift to paint background instead. [ ] size the brush, 1 2 3 pick the shape, Space pans.
backgroundAreas.hintUnmask: Paint over background to make it drivable again: brush by hand, drag a box, or draw a lasso around it.
backgroundAreas.hintLassoDrag: Hold the mouse and draw around the area.
backgroundAreas.hintRaw: Paint where roads should stay exactly as the elevation data has them, with no smoothing or levelling. Brush by hand, drag a box, or draw a lasso.
backgroundAreas.rawShift: Hold Shift to smooth again instead. [ ] size the brush, 1 2 3 pick the shape, Space pans.
backgroundAreas.hintRawOn: Roads here keep the terrain as downloaded.
backgroundAreas.statRaw: No smoothing on {pct}% of the square
backgroundAreas.lockedPinned: The area box is locked here so you can zoom and pan to draw (hold Space and drag to move the map with a tool picked).

build.title: What to build
build.presetHint_all: Everything the map has: roads, structures, buildings, street furniture, trees and water.
build.presetHint_clean: Everything except the clutter you hit while driving: benches, bins, hydrants, poles, gates, speed bumps and parked cars.
build.presetHint_roads: Roads with their markings, signs, lamps, bridges, tunnels and railways, on bare terrain.
build.presetHint_scenery: Terrain with trees, grass, rocks and water: no roads or buildings.
build.presetHint_custom: Your own choice of features below.
build.colourMapIn3d: What will be built is drawn on the 2D preview.

trees.title: Trees picked for this area
trees.fromClimate: No tree records around here: picked from the climate.
trees.note: For woods and trees the map doesn't name. A tree with a species in the map keeps it.
trees.switchHint: For each kind: keep it, leave it out (its trees are planted as the other kinds) or plant another kind in its place. Click a model to leave just that one out.

trees.modelOff: Left out: click to plant it again
trees.resetHint: Put every kind back to Keep and every model back on
